    <item>
      <title>Kraftig brann i Lillestrøm</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/stor-oslo/kraftig-brann-i-lillestrom-1.18081998</link>
      <description>Det brenner kraftig i en enebolig på en gård i Trondheimsveien i Lillestrøm.
– Det er full fyr i hele bygningen, opplyser oppdragsleder i politiet, Ronny Mangseth.
– Brannvesenet er fremme og er i gang med slukking. Det er kontroll på alle fire beboere på stedet, sier han.
Ved 17:20-tiden opplyser politiet at det fortsatt brenner kraftig i boligen, og at arbeidet med slukking vil ta tid.
En person skal ha fått i seg noe røyk.
Det skal ikke være fare for spredning til låve eller andre bygninger på gården.
Ifølge politiet er det ikke kjent hva som er årsaken til brannen.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Solbakken overrasker – Aasgaard inn i startelleveren</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/solbakken-overrasker-_-aasgaard-inn-i-startelleveren-1.18081988</link>
      <description>Ståle Solbakken har valgt ut følgende ellever til kampen mot Wales på Ullevaal:
Egil Selvik – Julian Ryerson, Kristoffer Ajer, Torbjørn Heggem, David Møller Wolfe – Sander Berge, Martin Ødegaard, Thelo Aasgaard – Antonio Nusa, Erling Braut Haaland, Oscar Bobb.
– Jeg må innrømme at jeg er noe overrasket. Men da tenker vel Solbakken at han passer bedre til denne kampen enn det Patrick Berg gjør akkurat nå, sier NRK-ekspert Andrine Hegerberg om at Aasgaards inntog i startelleveren.
Han er én av fire bytter som er gjort fra elleveren som møtte Portugal i forrige nasjonsligakamp.
Leo Østigård, Andreas Schjelderup og Patrick Berg er henvist til benken, mens Fredrik Aursnes ikke er med på grunn av en skade.
Samtidig er det nok en gang Egil Selvik som skal vokte buret for Norge.
– Jeg er først og fremst stolt, men også spent. Det blir en viktig kamp for oss, så det gjelder å gi jernet. Vi har noe å revansjere, sier Selvik til TV 2.
På motsatt banehalvdel starter Wales med følgende mannskap:
Karl Darlow – Neco Williams, Joe Rodon, Ben Davies, Jay Dasilva – Harry Wilson, Ethan Ampadu, Liam Cullen, Daniel James – Lewis Koumas, Brennan Johnson.</description>

      <description>En eldre kvinnelig bilfører kjørte ned tre personer i Lyngdal.

      <description>Britisk politi bekrefter overfor BBC at de har innledet en etterforskning mot komikeren David Walliams for alvorlige seksuelle forbrytelser.

      <description>Den tidligere Outlaws-sjefen og countrymusikeren er død, 82 år gammel, melder VG.
Holm Hansen ledet MC-klubben Outlaws, ble dømt for handel med narkotika og våpen og ga ut countrymusikk.
«Han sovnet stille inn på morgenen i dag, hjemme hos meg i sin egen seng, med venner og familie rundt seg», skriver datteren hans June Nordlie i et innlegg på Facebook.
Holm Hansen ble i 1981 dømt til 60 års fengsel i en kokainsak i USA, men ble besluttet deportert til Norge.
Selv hevdet han at dommen var et justismord, og knyttet saken til påstått arbeid for CIA.</description>

      <description>Nødetatene har fått melding om en skolebuss som har kjørt av veien i Larvik.
– Bussen har sklidd av veien og ut i grøfta med alle fire hjul. I bussen er det 24 barn som fremstår uskadd, skriver operasjonsleder Per Magne Eftang i politiloggen.
Bussjåføren er også uskadd, ifølge politiet.
– Barna er nå på vei ut av bussen og inn et hus for å holde varmen, sier Eftang til NRK.
Han sier alle barna brukte bilbelte.
Operasjonslederen antar at hendelsen kan knyttes til det glatte føret, men politiet har ikke kommet fram til stedet ennå.
Klokka 09.44 opplyser politiet at ingen er skadet. Flere foreldre har hentet barna sine og ny buss er klar til å frakte resten av barna til skolen.</description>

      <title>CNN: Demokratene vinner historisk senatsvalg i Mississippi</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/cnn_-demokratene-vinner-historisk-senatsvalg-i-mississippi-1.18079865</link>
      <description>Demokraten Scott Colom har vunnet senatsvalget i den tradisjonelt republikanske delstaten Mississippi, ifølge CNNs prognose.
Colom slår dermed den sittende republikanske senatoren Cindy Hyde-Smith, melder CNN onsdag kveld.
Han blir den første demokraten som representerer Mississippi i Senatet på over 40 år.
Colom blir også den første svarte politikeren som velges til et politisk verv av velgerne i hele Mississippi siden gjenoppbyggingsperioden etter den amerikanske borgerkrigen på 1800-tallet.
Valget ble holdt 3. november, men opptellingen har trukket ut i over en uke. Onsdag ettermiddag ledet Colom med rundt 3000 stemmer da om lag 98 prosent av stemmene var talt opp.
Resultatet er ennå ikke formelt godkjent. Fylkene i delstaten har frist til fredag med å godkjenne sine valgresultater.

      <description>Miljøpartiet de grønne (MDG) vil fremme et hasteforslag for å få satt kjøpet av Nussir-gruva på vent fram til nødvendige sikkerhetsvurderinger er gjennomført. Det opplyser partiet til NRK.

– Vi ønsker at regjeringa skal pause kjøpet fram til Stortinget eventuelt er overbevist om at dette ikke utgjør et sikkerhetsbrudd, sier Siren Jensen til NRK.
VG omtalte hasteforslaget først.
Nussir-gruva i Finnmark har store mengder kobber, men også gull og sølv.</description>

      <title>Trump: Nvidia-sjefen etterforskes av FBI</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/trump_-nvidia-sjefen-etterforskes-av-fbi-1.18077931</link>
      <description>Det føderale politiet FBI etterforsker Nvidia-sjef Jensen Huangs forhold til en kvinne som mistenkes for å ha spionert for Kina, sa president Donald Trump under en pressebriefing mandag kveld.
Trump sa også at Huang «ikke ante» at kvinnen angivelig er en kinesisk spion.
– Jeg stilte ham spørsmålet: 'Hadde du noen anelse om at hun var spion?' Han svarte: 'Jeg ante overhodet ikke at hun var spion,' og jeg tror ham virkelig, sa Trump.
Avsløringen av den 63 år gamle Nvidia-sjefens utenomekteskapelige forhold har rystet børsene, det politiske miljøet og teknologibransjen i USA.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Republikaner fremmer riksrettsforslag mot forsvarsminister Pete Hegseth</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/republikaner-fremmer-riksrettsforslag-mot-forsvarsminister-pete-hegseth-1.18077871</link>
      <description>Republikaneren Thomas Massie har levert et riksrettsforslag mot forsvarsminister Pete Hegseth i Representantenes hus.
Han varslet i september at han vil fremme riksrettsforslag mot Hegseth for maktmisbruk da Iran-krigen startet.
Massie er den republikaneren i Kongressen som i størst grad har kritisert president Donald Trump og hans nærmeste støttespillere.
Tidligere mandag sa Hegseth at han ikke var bekymret for riksrettsforslaget.
Ifølge New York Times må kongressen stemme over riksrettsforslaget innen to døgn.
(NRK/NTB)</description>

]]> 1361323 Immigrant medical specialists in B.C. see little improvement following licensing reforms https://cheknews.ca/immigrant-medical-specialists-in-b-c-see-little-improvement-following-licensing-reforms-1361235/ Sat, 14 Nov 2026 16:00:00 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1361235

The post Immigrant medical specialists in B.C. see little improvement following licensing reforms appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Vancouver resident Dr. Hassan Moustafa was hoping that recent changes to the BC College of Physicians and Surgeons licensing bylaws would give him a direct route to getting his career back as a general surgeon.

When that didn’t happen, his next best bet was to find a supervised associate physician position. So far, that has proven difficult.

Moustafa moved to Canada in 2017, after practising independently for seven years as a general surgeon. His previous roles included heading an emergency hospital in the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

But in Canada, he hasn’t been able to find a paying supervised position that matches his experience as a general surgeon.

“I am not asking to enter independent surgical practice without assessment or supervision,” Moustafa said.

The amended licensing bylaws, which came into effect July 6, allow eligible internationally trained physicians with recognized postgraduate qualifications to apply directly for a full medical licence instead of having to work first under a provisional licence.

In a news release announcing the province’s support for the changes, B.C.’s health ministry stated it would reduce paperwork and help eligible doctors begin independent practice sooner while maintaining patient care standards.

According to the College of Physicians and Surgeons of BC, eligibility depends on recognized postgraduate training and certification; Syria and Iraq are outside the approved jurisdictions for this direct licensing route.

Physicians with training from those countries must pursue other pathways, which may require further assessment, training or supervised employment.

In an emailed response to New Canadian Media, the College identified Australia, Ireland, the United Kingdom and the United States as recognized training jurisdictions for eligible family physicians. Specialists must have completed postgraduate training and hold a “completion-of-training certificate and specialty certification” from an approved jurisdiction. “Not all specialties are approved in each jurisdiction.”

The College of Family Physicians of Canada recognizes the same four countries because it considers their postgraduate family medicine training, accreditation and certification standards comparable to Canadian requirements.

A review published in July 2022 recommended continuing recognition of the same countries for family medicine. For specialists, Canada’s national certification body, the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons, maintains a separate approved jurisdiction route.

B.C.’s College of Physicians and Surgeons’ eligibility requirements consider where physicians complete their postgraduate training and the certification they hold, rather than their citizenship or birthplace. The July 2026 changes do not grant automatic licences to practise medicine.

Rosemary Pawliuk, president of the Society for Canadians Studying Medicine Abroad (SOCASMA), said licensing should depend on individual competence, not the country where a physician trained. Her organization helps Canadians educated overseas return to practise here.

Pawliuk said the changes have benefited many graduates of overseas medical schools, while immigrant physicians trained outside recognized jurisdictions continue to face barriers to assessment and training.

Meanwhile, staffing shortages continue to disrupt medical care in B.C. On Oct. 20, CJDC-TV reported that the District of Hudson’s Hope in northeastern B.C. experienced repeated shutdowns of its emergency department, which the region’s health authority attributed to staffing challenges.

B.C. is also recruiting overseas. A Sept. 21 health ministry release reported that 171 physicians, 445 nurses, 78 nurse practitioners, plus 44 allied health professionals had accepted jobs through its U.S. campaign.

Dr. Hassan Moustafa

Moustafa supports B.C.’s recruitment efforts, but said he also wants more opportunities for physicians already living in Canada.

During the pandemic, he worked as a COVID-19 tester for a Vancouver-based private health-care company. More recently, Moustafa travelled between Canada and Iraq to practise as a licensed general surgeon in the Kurdistan region because he has been unable to find a job in his specialty in Canada.

He said he is now focusing on remaining in Canada with his family and pursuing opportunities in surgery, patient safety and quality improvement.

“The biggest consequence has been lost professional income,” Moustafa said. “I have spent years unable to work as a surgeon in Canada.”

He said he has a profile with Health Match BC, a health-care recruitment service, and that his medical credentials have been verified with the institutions that issued them.

He has applied for associate physician roles and was interviewed for one general surgery position, but lost the job to another candidate.

“In several cases, I was told that there was clinical interest or need, but that funding for additional associate physician positions was limited, paused or unavailable,” he said.

Health Match BC’s published requirements are that associate physicians have employer sponsorship and work under supervision with accredited teams. These positions permit clinical work but not independent practice. To meet the criteria, a candidate has to find a suitable job as well as meet licensing requirements.

The Health Employers Association of British Columbia’s 2024-25 annual report stated that 106 associate physicians were working in B.C.

But Health Match BC said that number came from the B.C. College’s public directory for 2024-2025; it did not confirm how many associate physicians were actually working and does not collect data on funded, filled or vacant associate physician positions in province.

The directory also doesn’t distinguish immigrant physicians already living in B.C. from Canadians educated abroad or recruited from overseas.

Mervat Bazary, a Syrian specialist who arrived in Canada in 2023, is working to rebuild her career.

She practised as an ear, nose and throat specialist for 10 years before moving to B.C, then spent two years improving her English. She has recently enrolled at Douglas College in New Westminster, B.C. in a hearing instrument practitioner diploma program.

Eligible international medical school graduates can also look for residencies to complete the requirements to practise medicine in Canada. In B.C., the University of B.C.’s Clinical Assessment Program assesses international medical graduates seeking residency training in the province.

This group includes immigrant doctors as well as Canadians who studied medicine abroad. UBC reported 360 assessment participants in 2023; 358 in 2024; and 352 in 2025. The number doesn’t reflect how many applied for residency positions.

Doctors who successfully complete the assessment program can apply for residency positions through the Canadian Resident Matching Service.

The UBC Faculty of Medicine stated that the number of dedicated entry-level international medical graduates positions have increased from 18 to 58 since 2010. It said all of those positions, which are funded by B.C.’s health ministry, are filled every year.

In 2024, B.C. added another 20 entry-level positions that are open to eligible Canadian and international medical school graduates.

Influence Board Shop hopes to trade profits for purpose, keeping its doors open as a hub for skateboarding, youth development and community connection.

On a grey, rainy day in Victoria, an empty skate park is nothing unusual. But at Influence Board Shop on Quadra Street, the quiet reflects something bigger: a business preparing for a major change.

After 15 years as a fixture in Victoria’s skateboarding community, Influence is looking to transition into a non-profit organization.

Owner Steve Munro says the skateboarding retail business has taken a hit in recent years.

“The skateboarding business, as I know and everyone else in my industry knows, has really gone down dramatically in the last few years,” he says.

Rather than give up the space, Munro is looking to change the business model and its purpose.

“We’re trying to pivot into a non-profit kind of formula, and just kind of open up this space, not to make money because that’s never really been our goal.”

The property includes a retail shop, three indoor skate parks, a stage for all-ages shows and a planned café. Munro wants to make those facilities more accessible, with a focus on health and recreation, youth development and community improvement.

A non-profit structure could also open the door to funding opportunities, including youth sports grants.

But first, the resident director of boards needs a board of directors, among other things. He’s looking for volunteers with professional experience who are willing to lend their skills to the cause.

“We’re looking for volunteers as far as someone who knows law, someone who knows accounting,” he says.

The bigger ambition is to give back to a community that has changed his life and make skateboarding more welcoming to everyone, including newcomers who may not know a kickflip from a kickstand.

For regulars like Dylon, the space is already making a difference. He’s recently returned to skateboarding and now visits twice a week.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

“Started getting back into it, coming here two times a week now,” he says.

Asked if he’s hooked, his answer is emphatic: “I’m hooked!”

Munro says the skateboarding community has always been supportive, despite the sport’s sometimes rebellious reputation. And with skateboarding now an Olympic sport, he thinks perceptions are changing.

“Now that we’re in the Olympics, we’re not really the bad guys in TV shows anymore. We’re kinda the good guys,” he says with a smile.

For now, the ramps will stay busy, the boards will keep rolling and the shop will continue.

Business as usual.

Whether the proposed non-profit transition succeeds remains to be seen. But after 15 years, Influence is hoping its next chapter will be less about business and more about giving back.

As Canada’s most prolific voyeur serves prison time for victimizing more than 600 women and girls across the capital region, the surreptitious non-consensual images Derek Yin Yeung Chan took and uploaded online, continue to spread.

“You could find Chan’s Reddit account and a post with 19 images of women and girls shopping in Greater Victoria,” said Emily Fagan, a CBC associate producer who found Chan’s Reddit posts by searching his account names found in court documents.

“A lot of the video show women, especially young girls, being followed. The photos specifically show young women or girls…not realizing that they’re being photographed while they’re shopping,” said Fagan. “There’s the appearance that the person taking the photos is trying to shoot down their clothing, and in some cases, successfully.”

In the images, Fagan says she recognized innocuous everyday Greater Victoria places that no one would expect being secretly, inappropriately, filmed: Winners, Value Village, what appeared to be Mayfair Mall, Walmart and a Shoppers Drug Mart.

Fagan says the post was tagged “NSFW”, meaning not safe for work. In the comments Fagan says Chan was telling people more images were available for people who paid.

Despite being convicted in May, Chan’s Reddit posts and account were active until September 2026.

‘Unprecedented” scale

In May, Chan, 39, was sentenced to 4.5 years in prison for convictions of voyeurism, making child pornography, publishing recordings obtained through a crime, and breaching court ordered conditions.

Saanich Police began investigating Chan after a January 2024 tip flagged that an account in Saanich was uploading voyeuristic images. That account brought police to Chan.

At the time, Chan had already been convicted for filming a woman in Uptown’s Forever 21 change room in 2019, telling psychologists at the time he did it for an “adrenaline rush” roughly 20 times, and promised to stop.

He didn’t, and Chan’s behaviour seems to have escalated.

He began filming underage girls, and women across the capital region through their home windows, at the beach, up their skirts or down their shirts while they shopped, before posting the non-consensual intimate images online for the consumption of strangers.

Police believe there to be 652 separate victims, 64 were underage, only 40 victims were successfully identified.

“There is an extreme amount of victims here. This case is very significant. The words like unprecedented certainly come to mind,” said Saanich Police Deputy Chief Damian Kowalewich told CHEK News in May.

The judge who sentenced Chan quantified the amount of images as “countless”.

Why were the images still on Reddit?

Fagan found the photos on Reddit in August, roughly three months after Chan was sentenced to prison. She reached out to Reddit, which didn’t respond.

A month later, when the Canadian Centre for Child Protection reached out “within hours”, Fagan says Chan’s posts were deleted and his account was banned.

Lloyd Richardson, the Centre for Child Protection’s director of technology says, “you’re failing if you’ve missed that.”

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

“It really highlights the problem there. They should be dealing with these. They’re clearly not staffing their trust and safety staff properly and we see this across the board with the big tech companies.”

CHEK News reached out asking if Reddit’s moderation safeguards failed in this case but didn’t receive a response.

Richardson says Bill C-34, the Safe Social Media Act that’s making it’s way through the House of Commons right now, would keep big tech in line in these scenarios.

“It’s the first massive step in a long set of steps that we need to take,” said Richardson. “This should have been in place over a decade ago. The fact that essentially tech companies have been unregulated since the birth of the internet and have gotten worse progressively, it’s insane we’re only doing this now.”

Images found elsewhere, just the tip of the iceberg

Using image matching technology called Project Arachnid, the Canadian Centre for Child Protection found duplicates of the Reddit images online elsewhere, on forums dedicated to sharing non-consensual type imagery, and other chat rooms.

But those 19 Reddit images are just the tip of the iceberg.

“I imagine there’s probably a bunch of victims that don’t even know they’re victims in this case because of the sheer volume,” said Richardson.

Despite attempts by Saanich Police to get them taken down, the majority of those “countless” images are still out there and continuing to cause harm.

In 2011, the Conservatives swept the federal election, with the exception of the riding of Saanich-Gulf Islands.

Federal Green Party leader Elizabeth May defeated former Conservative cabinet minister Gary Lunn.

That night, CHEK News reporter Dana Hutchins asked May if she had a message to her Saanich-Gulf Islands voters.

“Thank-you, thank-you, thank-you. Bless you and thank-you. I will work tirelessly to earn and deserve the trust you put in me today,” May said.

And she’s held the riding ever since.

“I’ve got more than a full-time job as the member for Saanich-Gulf Islands. It’s definitely, I’m working seven days a week, and long days. But I’m so excited,” May said from her home in Ottawa.

She retires as party leader on Saturday, when the new leader will be announced. But she’s not leaving federal politics. She’s staying on as MP.

READ RELATED: Two candidates running for Green Party leadership, winner to be announced Nov. 14

“I’m doing everything I can to make sure that I’ll be running again whenever the next federal election is,” May said.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

Canadians got their first chance to see May in action during the 2008 leaders’ debate.

“To decide if you lost something you don’t like or contract something you don’t like, you just sweep it across the table don’t you,” May said to then federal Conservative Party of Canada leader Stephen Harper.

She says participating in it was critical.

“The single most important thing is getting in the national leaders debate; When I started in parliament, I was only the second Green in the world to get elected in the first-past-the-post system. I was never imagining that I would be the Member of Parliament in 2026 for Saanich Gulf Islands,” May said.

Dr. Kimberly Speers, associate professor for the School of Public Administration with the University of Victoria says May’s 2011 election helped bring environmental issues to the forefront of Canadian politics.

“That win in 2011 demonstrated as well that Canadians were becoming more interested about environmental politics as well. And felt that it was important for an mp a political party, and other political parties to pay attention to,” Speers said.

Former B.C. Green MLA Adam Olsen says May’s legacy is the path she forged for the Green Party candidates who followed her.

“For a long time the Greens were on the outside looking in to legislatures, and House of Hommons. And with Elizabeth’s election it sent a message. That where you have a quality candidate someone who is willing to stand up and speak truth to power, stand up and represent their constituents, that there is a pathway for them to be elected in Canada and British Columbia,” Olsen said.

Mike Morrice is the new federal leader, and May says she’ll work hard for her constituents as their MP for as long as they elect her.
